content.comment_body: Hello, I would like to connect several IR sensors to a [product_name] [version_no]. These sensors are originally intended for use with Arduino boards and provide digital outputs at 3.3V or 5V. [url] I am completely new to using [product_name] and would appreciate any guidance to get started.
No. The output signal is a PWM type, which isn't compatible with [product_name].

Apologies for the earlier incorrect answer. After personally testing a sensor module I ordered, I found that it does work with [product_name]. You can connect it directly to an analog input (0-10VDC). When no object is detected, the module outputs about 4.5VDC; when something enters the range, it drops to roughly 0.2-0.3VDC. This change can be monitored with an analog threshold. If you want to use a digital input, you’ll need an optocoupler because [product_name] recognizes voltages below 5VDC as a 0-signal. To register a 1-signal on a digital input, it requires at least 12VDC. I powered the module using a 5VDC regulator connected to the 24VDC supply for [product_name].

analysis.insight_summary: A beginner is seeking help to connect digital IR sensors, originally designed for Arduino, to a [product_name] input module. Initial feedback mistakenly claimed incompatibility, but after hands-on testing, helpful instructions clarified how to successfully interface these sensors to both analog and digital inputs, highlighting important voltage-level considerations for proper functionality.
